name: AI virtual staging and photo enhancement for estate agents
one_liner: Use an AI image editor (Nano Banana / Gemini) to make listing photos look staged or professionally shot, then offer per-photo work to agents by sending them a free edited sample of their own listing first.
customer: Estate agents and property sellers with unstaged or poor-quality listing photos
offer: Per-photo AI virtual staging and photo upgrades, starting with a free sample of a live listing
how_it_makes_money: About $1 per photo charged against about $0.04 AI cost (the video quotes a 96% margin), roughly $20 per listing, with the aim of winning all of an agent's current and future listings
startup_cost: low: a vibe-coded web app plus AI API costs
time_to_first_revenue: days to weeks (the video is a demand test, not a proven revenue case)
evidence: 'about 70% of them list homes for sale that either have bad pictures or pictures of homes that aren't staged' (_mWhcH41Mxw)
'homes that are staged... sell for 6 to 10% more' (_mWhcH41Mxw)
'charge you a buck per photo... 96% profit margin' (_mWhcH41Mxw)
risks: Very low price, so it needs volume or a subscription
Low barrier to entry; listing portals or tools may add this themselves
UK and PT advertising rules require virtual staging to be disclosed
Unsolicited texting/outreach rules (PECR/GDPR)

name: AI pitch decks for newly registered funds and startups
one_liner: Find new fund launches in public filings, then send the managers a congratulations message, a portfolio, and an offer to build a pitch deck quickly with AI.
customer: New fund managers and founders who have just made a public filing
offer: A done-for-you pitch deck, with AI drafting and a human polishing it
how_it_makes_money: Fixed project fee: the 'pitch deck guy' cited charges $3,500 per deck
startup_cost: low: AI tools plus filing data or an API
tools: SEC EDGAR filings (UK: Companies House / FCA register)
evidence: 'He goes and he scrapes SEC filings when people launch a new fund... What does he charge? 3500 bucks.' (_uHy0zY9hgk)
'Sell These $3.5K AI Pitch Decks Built in 12 Min' (_uHy0zY9hgk)
risks: Evidence is a single anecdote about one Twitter operator
Quality and design skill decide the price
The UK equivalent of the filing trigger needs to be confirmed

name: White-label HighLevel SaaS for one niche
one_liner: Rebrand HighLevel (CRM, SMS, AI voice agents, funnels) as your own software for one industry and charge each client a monthly fee.
customer: Small businesses in one niche, e.g. estate agents, that don't know these tools exist
offer: Branded CRM, texting, automation and AI receptionist software for that niche
how_it_makes_money: Monthly subscription per sub-account; the example is about 500 customers giving about $100k/month (roughly $200 each)
evidence: 'They've got over 500 customers... That's $100,000 a month' (_b5kM2zDQTk)
'gold SaaSpreneur award... over 100 sub accounts, which means you have over 100 customers' (_b5kM2zDQTk)
risks: Depends on one platform and its pricing
Churn and support load
A crowded market for English-language niches; Portuguese-language markets may be less crowded

name: Cold-email-led B2B lead generation and lead lists
one_liner: Use scraped lead lists and 10–15-step cold email sequences to win customers for a B2B offer, or sell the lead lists and campaigns themselves.
customer: B2B service and software firms that need meetings
offer: Scraped lead lists and managed cold email campaigns
how_it_makes_money: Retainer or per-lead/per-meeting pricing, or selling lead data (exact prices not stated)
startup_cost: low: you can start at about 100 emails a month
time_to_first_revenue: 'You can get your first customer in a day'
evidence: 'first 1 million ARR almost entirely through cold email' (Zpu-eL-PToU)
'75 plus percent of the revenue... is not from the first email' (Zpu-eL-PToU)
Will Cannon is 'an expert in scraping and selling leads' with two multi-million software businesses (bH_coG-2ASo)
risks: Weak evidence for selling this as a service; the proof is cold email used as an acquisition channel
Deliverability problems
UK/EU rules (PECR, GDPR) on B2B email and scraped data

name: Programmatic SEO directory sites
one_liner: Build AI-generated directory sites that rank on Google for long-tail searches, then copy the template to new niches.
customer: Advertisers, affiliate partners and listed businesses
how_it_makes_money: Ads, affiliate commissions, paid listings (no specific revenue stated)
evidence: '$0 paid on advertising, costing basically nothing to build. This is all the pages we're ranking number one for.' (abeY8nBzqzo)
'If I could right click, duplicate. 10 seconds.' (abeY8nBzqzo)
risks: Google penalties for low-quality AI content
No monetisation figures given (weak evidence)
Slow to reach cash

name: Washer and dryer rentals via Facebook Marketplace
one_liner: Rent out refurbished second-hand washers and dryers monthly to local renters, finding customers on Facebook Marketplace.
offer: Monthly appliance rental including delivery and installation
how_it_makes_money: About $40/month per machine; reaches profit by month 2; free used machines fixed up for about $30; example is $10k/month on 5 hours a week
startup_cost: low-medium: used appliances and a van
time_to_first_revenue: first week ($350 a week of recurring revenue in the replication)
evidence: '22 years old, zero employees, 5 hours per week, making $10,000 a month' (aXVM-HI388g)
'$1,200 to $1,500 in recurring revenue month one' (aXVM-HI388g)
risks: Requires physical work in person
UK rentals often come with appliances or are small flats, so demand is unproven
Repairs and non-payment

name: Stump grinding as a subcontractor for tree surgeons
one_liner: Grind stumps for tree companies that don't offer the service, getting work through referrals instead of ads.
how_it_makes_money: $200 minimum per job; $32k revenue in the first 2 months; one contractor referred $25k of work in 4–5 months
startup_cost: medium: grinder and trailer (can be rented first); equipment keeps its value
time_to_first_revenue: immediate (he made $9k before quitting his job)
evidence: 'I have a $200 minimum. 200 bucks for 5 minutes of work' (awzWbwtmOd4)
'70k in revenue before... I even had to Google my business' (awzWbwtmOd4)
risks: Manual, local work
Doesn't fit the async-first goal
Safety and insurance
